program_narrative: Program DB2HNDL is a batch template that demonstrates the standard pattern for DB2 access against the PORTFOLIO table; it works on hard-coded example data rather than input files. It connects to the database 'sample', inserts a test portfolio row ('PORT00001', 'TEST PORTFOLIO', status 'A', value 0), reads it back with a singleton SELECT, opens a cursor over all active portfolios and fetches rows until no more rows remain, marks the test portfolio inactive with an UPDATE, deletes it, and finally commits and disconnects. After each INSERT/SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE and after CONNECT, a common check routine displays any non-zero SQLCODE with its error text; a negative SQLCODE triggers a ROLLBACK, sets return code 8, runs the termination (COMMIT and disconnect) and ends the program. Gaps: the per-row cursor handler 2310-PROCESS-CURSOR-ROW does not exist in the program, the cursor statements themselves are not checked, and the SQLCA fields SQLCODE/SQLERRMC are not defined in the registered SQLCA copybook.

paragraphs.name: 9000-CHECK-SQL-STATUS
pseudocode: IF SQLCODE != 0 THEN  -- the last SQL statement returned a warning or an error
SET sqlcode_display = SQLCODE  -- edited picture -999 for display
SET sql_error_text = SQLERRMC  -- DB2 error message tokens
DISPLAY db2_error_message  -- 'DB2 ERROR - SQLCODE: ' + code + ', SQLERRM: ' + text
IF SQLCODE < 0 THEN  -- error (positive codes such as +100 are warnings)
CALL 9100-rollback
SET return_code = 8  -- RETURN-CODE special register
CALL 3000-terminate  -- COMMIT WORK and CONNECT RESET
RETURN to caller  -- GOBACK inside the error branch ends the program
END IF
END IF
